claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has high caloric performance.
The as-cast alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
A coarse or inhomogeneous microstructure causes the alloy's poor integrity and cracking tendency.
Annealing near 700 °C for 2–15 minutes can induce partial recrystallization in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Brief annealing will refine the microstructure of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Partial recrystallization will produce a high fraction of low-angle grain boundaries.
Annealing will produce a more homogeneous phase distribution in the target alloy.
Refined boundaries and a more homogeneous phase distribution will reduce stress concentrations associated with crack initiation.
Limiting annealing to partial recrystallization will avoid complete grain coarsening.
The partially recrystallized microstructure will improve toughness and mechanical integrity.
Controlled annealing will preserve the key phase composition responsible for the caloric effect.
The annealed alloy will have greater compressive strength than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will have greater ductility and lower cracking susceptibility than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy's magnetocaloric or barocaloric response will remain within approximately 10% of the untreated alloy's response.
Longer annealing can lead to larger grains and near-complete recrystallization.
Complete recrystallization or grain growth could diminish the intrinsic caloric effect or cause undesired phase transformations.

A successful treatment should yield at least an approximately 30% increase in compressive strength or a marked improvement in crack resistance while retaining caloric response within approximately 10% of the as-cast value.
